newsitem.title: CHINA: China suspends rubber futures trading for one day.
newsitem.headline: China suspends rubber futures trading for one day.

text.p: The China Commodity Futures Exchange in southern Hainan province on Wednesday temporarily suspended trading in rubber futures contracts to hold a one-day meeting on market risk, the exchange said in a statement.
Trading in the August 1997 contract has given rise to "huge risks," and the exchange decided to hold an emergency meeting to discuss the matter, the statement said.
Trading in rubber futures would resume on Thursday, it said.
The key August contract had fluctuated sharply as investors who were long or short in the market tried to make the price favour their positions.
The August contract then fell sharply after the exchange introduced crackdown measures, including raising margin requirements and banning investors from building new positions.
The August contract closed limit-down on Tuesday at 11,700 yuan ($1,411) per tonne, down 401 yuan from Monday's close.
